messages.content: What is the total distance in kilometers if you were to travel from the Eiffel Tower in Paris (48.8584° N, 2.2945° E) to the Colosseum in Rome (41.8902° N, 12.4922° E), then to the Acropolis in Athens (37.9715° N, 23.7257° E), and finally to the Pyramids of Giza in Egypt (29.9792° N, 31.1342° E)?

function.name: calculate_distance
function.description: Calculate the distance between two GPS coordinates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

unit.description: The unit of distance. Defaults to miles if not specified.

message.content:
**Step‑by‑step calculation**

The most accurate way to get “straight‑line” (great‑circle) distances between two sets of geographic coordinates is the **Haversine / spherical law of cosines** formula  

\[
d \;=\; R\,\theta ,
\qquad 
\theta \;=\;\arccos(\sin\varphi_1\!\sin\varphi_2+\cos\varphi_1\!\cos\varphi_2\!\cos\Delta\lambda)
\]

where  
\(R = 6371\text{ km}\) – Earth’s mean radius,  
\((\varphi,\lambda)\) – latitude & longitude in **radians**,  
and \(\Delta\lambda\) is the longitudinal separation.

Below are the intermediate values for each leg of your journey.

| Leg | Start (deg) | End (deg) | Δϕ (rad) | Δλ (rad) | θ (rad) | Distance (km) |
|-----|-------------|-----------|----------|----------|---------|---------------|
| Eiffel → Colosseum | \(48.8584^\circ , 2.2945^\circ\) | \(41.8902^\circ , 12.4922^\circ\) | ‑0.1211 | 0.1779 | 0.1859 | **1 184 km** |
| Colosseum → Acropolis | \(41.8902^\circ , 12.4922^\circ\) | \(37.9715^\circ , 23.7257^\circ\) | ‑0.0679 | 0.1963 | 0.1789 | **1 141 km** |
| Acropolis → Pyramids | \(37.9715^\circ , 23.7257^\circ\) | \(29.9792^\circ , 31.1342^\circ\) | ‑0.1401 | 0.1295 | 0.1815 | **1 156 km** |

---

### Total distance

Adding the three legs together:

\[
\boxed{
1\,184\ \text{km}
+
1\,141\ \text{km}
+
1\,156\ \text{km}
=
3\,481\ \text{km}
}
\]

> **Approximately 3 500 kilometres** will be travelled when moving directly (as the crow flies) from the Eiffel Tower ➜ Colosseum ➜ Acropolis ➜ Pyramids of Giza. 

*(All figures rounded to whole kilometres.)*
